newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia hopes to lead by example at APEC meeting.
newsitem.headline: Australia hopes to lead by example at APEC meeting.

text.p: Australia hopes to lead by example with a trade action plan it will present to the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum meeting in the Philippines, Trade Minister Tim Fischer said on Tuesday.

But Canberra, detailing an Individual Action Plan (IAP) that exceeded its obligations to other APEC meetings, expected only modest results from the meeting as part of a progressive process, Fischer told Parliament.

"...Australia will be seeking, through the IAP process, to use the liberalisation of the Australian economy to argue for enhanced market of interest to Australian exporters in other APEC economies," Fischer said.
"I expect modest outcomes, as this year is only the beginning of the process," he said.
APEC members agreed in Osaka last year to detail progress on trade liberalisation in public action plans.
But Australia, always urging other APEC members to go faster, has for years pursued a programme of microeconomic reform that goes beyond trade obligations to other countries.

For example, Fischer detailed in Australia's action plan a commitment to introduce full and open competition in telecommunications from July 1997, which has been Australian policy since well before APEC countries committed themselves in 1994 to liberalisation.
But the minister emphasised that no great progress could be expected from 1996 alone.
"There has been a gradual improvement in the quality of (APEC members') IAPs during the year," he said.
"I expect that the 1996 IAPs will represent a modest improvement in access for Australian exporters and will illustrate the wide range of liberalisation underway in the region," Fischer said.
APEC members have agreed to liberalise the region's economy by the year 2010 in the case of developed members and by 2020 for developing members.
APEC officials and ministers will meet starting on Wednesday in Manila. The heads of state and governments of the 18 APEC members will meet in Subic on November 25.
